nodes.title: Absolute-height calculus from relative heights
nodes.statement: For a number field K of degree D and x,y∈K, h(x)=NumberField.absLogHeight₁ x satisfies h(x⁻¹)=h(x), h(x^n)=|n|h(x) for n∈ℤ, h(xy)≤h(x)+h(y), and h(x+y)≤log 2+h(x)+h(y). For a∈ℤ, h(a)=log(max(1,|a|)). The same values hold after a characteristic-zero field embedding.
hypotheses: K is a number field; D=[K:ℚ]>0.
For an ambient field version, all arguments are algebraic over ℚ.
proofSteps: Use DT.0’s extension normalization to write h_K(x)=Height.logHeight₁ x/D.
Divide the pinned inversion, power, product and sum formulas by D; NumberField.totalWeight_eq_finrank cancels D in the sum constant.
Restrict an integer to ℚ and use Rat.logHeight₁_eq_log_max; transport by DT.0’s embedding comparison.

nodes.title: Subgroups, tangent spaces and dimensions in the one-torus case
nodes.statement: Every algebraic subgroup H⊂K^d×Kˣ is uniquely V×T, where V is a linear subspace and T is either Kˣ or μN for some N≥1. Its ideal is generated by V⊥ and, in the finite case, Y^N−1. The neutral component is V×Kˣ or V×{1}; TeH is V×K or V×{0}, respectively. If r=dim V, then 𝓗(V×Kˣ;D)=2(r+1)D0^rD1 and 𝓗(V×μN;D)=N D0^r.
hypotheses: K is algebraically closed and characteristic zero; H is a reduced algebraic subgroup.

proofSteps: Specialize Proposition 5.6 to one multiplicative coordinate: distinct characters and translations force the proposed ideal.
Use the rank-one subgroup classification of ℤ, then the squarefreeness of Y^N−1 for the components.

nodes.title: Wüstholz’s transverse multiplicity inequality
nodes.statement: Let E be a finite nonempty union of cosets of an algebraic subgroup H⊂Gd, J=I(E), and A an ideal all of whose elements vanish through order S0 along W at every point of E. If dim Z(A)=dim H and ℓ=dim((W+TeH)/TeH), then 𝓗(A;D)≥binom(S0+ℓ,ℓ)𝓗(E;D).
hypotheses: K is algebraically closed of characteristic zero; A is proper and S0≥0.
The support dimension equality is essential; no inequality between leading forms of different total degrees is asserted.
proofSteps: Choose ℓ directions in W and subgroup equations with derivative-pairing matrix the identity modulo I(H); obtain coset versions using squared Chinese-remainder selectors.
Leibniz and factorials show D^β(PQ^α) is zero modulo J for |β|≤|α| unless β=α, when it is α!P.
Take a bounded-degree complement to J. Its products with Q^α for |α|≤S0 are independent modulo A, by the least derivative order and characteristic zero.
Compare quotient dimensions at D+S0C and pass to their top homogeneous parts.

nodes.title: Roy’s relative multiplicity estimate for one torus
nodes.statement: Let H−⊂H+⊂Gd be connected algebraic subgroups, d+=dim H+>0, Σ⊂H+ contain the identity, W⊂TeH+, S0≥0, and P of filtration bound D not identically zero on H+. If P vanishes through order d+·S0 along W on Σ[d+]+H−, there is a connected proper subgroup H*⊂H+ containing H−, with ℓ=dim((W+TeH*)/TeH*), such that binom(S0+ℓ,ℓ)#((Σ+H*)/H*)𝓗(H*;D)≤𝓗(H+;D). H* can be chosen as a component cut out in H+ by polynomials of bound D.
hypotheses: K is algebraically closed of characteristic zero; all degree bounds are nonnegative integers.
Σ[r] is the set of sums of r elements; Σ[0] is the identity.
The cardinality in the conclusion is finite.
proofSteps: Form the nested ideals generated by bounded-degree derivatives and translates. Their zero-set dimensions have a plateau within d+ steps.
An irreducible component at that plateau has an algebraic stabilizer; the translates contained in the preceding zero set form a finite union of its cosets.
The transporter is cut out by bounded-degree translates, so the complete-intersection upper bound applies; use transverse-jet-multiplicity-bound for the lower bound.
Pass to the neutral component without changing its tangent space. Enlarge Σ by H−; connectedness forces H− into the resulting subgroup.

nodes.title: Vanishing order of a partially analytic alternant
nodes.statement: Let fi(z)=pi(z)φi(θ·z), pi a polynomial in n variables of degree≤T0, φi entire. In an L-row determinant, choose analytic rows I, evaluate each at finitely many zζμ after differential operators of order≤S0, and allow a constant rectangular column change Q. All other rows are constant. Its scalar entire determinant DI has order at zero at least max(0,Θ(n,T0,#I)−L S0). Consequently |DI(1)|≤E^(−max(0,Θ−LS0)) sup|z|=E |DI(z)| for E>1.

proofSteps: Make a linear coordinate change aligning θ with the first coordinate; if θ=0 the polynomial case is immediate.
Expand φi into Taylor series. Equal surviving monomials in two analytic rows kill the determinant; their distinct degrees cost at least Θ.
Each differential operator loses at most S0 degrees. The column change does not alter the argument.
Taylor factorization converts the order into the little-o hypothesis of the pinned radius-ratio Schwarz theorem; bound the circle supremum by the maximum principle.

nodes.title: Full rank after the minimal-subspace selection
nodes.statement: Let S⊂ℤ^m be finite, S̃=S−S, vβ=(β1,…,βm−1,−1), and V⊂K^m a d-dimensional subspace containing vβ. Assume the first m−d coordinate vectors project to a basis of K^m/V, the αj generate a multiplicative group of rank≥m−1, S0+1≥2T0, |sj|<T0/4 for s∈S, and either β0≠0 or S̃[2]∩K vβ={0}. Assume (S0+1)#S>2(m+1)T0^mT1, #πV(S)≤(m+1)/(d+1)T0^(m−d), and no proper V′⊂V containing vβ satisfies the same quotient bound with d′. Then the modified matrix with σ≤(m+1)S0 and s∈(S̃∩V)[m+1] has row rank binom(T0+d,d)(2T1+1).
hypotheses: K is algebraically closed of characteristic zero; 1≤d≤m; T0,T1,S0 are positive integers.
S̃[r] is an r-fold sum of the difference set, not the original set S.
proofSteps: A rank failure gives a nonzero bounded-degree Laurent polynomial with the specified invariant-jet zeros.

Apply Roy’s relative estimate to Ga^d×Gm; injectivity of s↦sy follows from the stated β-direction condition. For D=∂X0+Y∂Y use W=K·(1,0,…,0,1). Its torus coordinate is 1; the direction printed in the author PDF p.282 has an erroneous final 0 (E610), while p.283 uses the required final 1.
Classify the obstruction subgroup. A finite torus obstruction contradicts multiplicative rank and the box bound; a full torus obstruction gives a proper V′ with the forbidden quotient cardinality.
A largest fiber of S→K^m/V supplies the needed # (S̃∩V) inequality.

Its β total degree is≤LT0, each αj/αj⁻¹ block degree is≤LT1Sj, and its length is bounded by L! times the product of the cleared row-entry length bounds from Lemma 9.11. nodes.title: Hermite interpolation with a p-adic denominator bound
nodes.statement: Let p,q be distinct primes, q|R, R,M≥1, θ>0 rational, and a∈E with vp(a)=θ. Put I={s∈ℤ:1≤s≤R,q∤s}, N=M#I=(1−1/q)RM, A=Nθ+Mvp(R!)+(M−1)log R/log p. For any prescribed jets jt,s in E, 0≤t<M, there is a unique polynomial Q of degree<N with Q^(t)(sa)/t!=jt,s. If vp(jt,s)+tθ≥A for all s,t, each coefficient ck of Q satisfies vp(ck)+kθ≥Nθ. In particular ck is integral because k<N, Q is normal, and vp(Q(ya))≥Nθ for every p-integral y.
hypotheses: E is a complete p-adic field containing a; zero jets have infinite order.
The interpolation derivatives are normalized by t!; nodes sa are pairwise distinct.
proofSteps: Use the Chinese remainder decomposition E[z]/∏s(z−sa)^M and choose its unique representative of degree<N.
Write each Hermite basis term as (z−sa)^t times ∏r≠s((z−ra)/(sa−ra))^M times the appropriate truncated inverse at sa.
Count the p-power denominators of products of integer differences: their cost is at most Mvp(R!)+(M−1)log R/log p. The powers of a add at most (N−t)θ.
The coefficient of degree k in a basis term for the t-th jet has order at least (t−k)θ−Mvp(R!)−(M−1)log R/log p. The jet hypothesis therefore gives vp(ck)+kθ≥Nθ after summation.

nodes.title: Yu’s normal-function extrapolation lemma
nodes.statement: With the primes, integers, θ and a of hermite-interpolation-denominator-bound, let F be normal. If min_{s∈I,0≤t<M}(vp(F^(t)(sa)/t!)+tθ)≥Nθ+Mvp(R!)+(M−1)log R/log p, then for every k∈ℤ, vp(F((k/q)a))≥Nθ, where N=(1−1/q)RM.
hypotheses: θ>0, M,R≥1, q|R, q≠p, and vp(a)=θ.
All evaluated coordinates are integral since q is a p-adic unit.
proofSteps: Form the Hermite interpolant Q. Its strengthened jet budget bounds Q((k/q)a) by order≥Nθ using its basis formula.
The difference F−Q has order≥M at every sa. Divide by their M-th-power product within normal functions.
At (k/q)a every difference from a node has order≥θ. The product has order≥Nθ and the normal quotient is integral.
Apply the ultrametric inequality to Q plus the product remainder.

sources.match: The exact factorial and logarithmic losses in the jet hypothesis.

sources.locator: Chapter I §4, Lemma 1.4 and its proof, pp.18–26

acceptance: The conclusion concerns every integer k, including q-divisible ones.

nodes.title: Finite-place Liouville for integer polynomials
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree D, P above p with residue degree f, and F∈ℤ[X1,…,Xr] have length L≥1 and degree≤Nj in Xj. For βj∈K, F(β)≠0 implies ordP(F(β))≤D/(f log p)(log L+Σj Nj h(βj)). Dividing by e gives the normalized vp bound.
hypotheses: The polynomial coefficients are rational integers; the evaluation is nonzero.
Negative exponents must first be represented with inverse variables, using equal inverse height.
proofSteps: Bound the local evaluation at all other places by length and the separate scalar heights.
At P isolate its negative log contribution in the global product formula.
Use vP=(p^f)^−ordP and the absolute-height normalization.

sources.match: The evaluation bound converts an analytic high-order estimate to exact zero.

acceptance: For F=X−1, β=1+p^k over ℚ the inequality is k≤log(2(1+p^k))/log p.
A zero evaluation is excluded, rather than assigned a finite order.

nodes.title: An explicit one-power bound over a number field
nodes.statement: For α∈Kˣ, b∈ℤ nonzero, α^b≠1, and P above p of ramification e and residue degree f, ordP(α^b−1)≤D/(f log p){log(2|b|)+(p^f−1)(1+1/(p−1))e h(α)}, where D=[K:ℚ].
hypotheses: K is a number field; p is prime; α^b≠1.
No unit or non-torsion assumption is imposed on α.
proofSteps: If ordPα≠0, the left side is≤0. If α is torsion, apply finite-place Liouville to its nontrivial torsion power minus 1.
For a non-torsion unit take its residue order s≤p^f−1 and then the least κ bringing α^(sp^κ) into vp>1/(p−1); its minimality gives p^κ≤(1+1/(p−1))e.
Use deep-unit-exp-log-adapter to identify vp((α^(sp^κ))^b−1)=vp(b)+vp(α^(sp^κ)−1).
Apply finite-place Liouville and h(α^(sp^κ))=sp^κhα, then ef≤D and vp(b)≤log|b|/log p.

sources.match: This separate lemma supplies the length-one reduction without padding an unproved full-Kummer hypothesis.

acceptance: The p=2 threshold is strict and requires the extra power when necessary.
For a nonunit the positive right side bounds a nonpositive order.

nodes.title: Polynomial rows in the relative Siegel bound
nodes.statement: Let K/ℚ have degree D, γij=Pij(β1,…,βr) with Pij∈ℤ[X], degrees in Xk bounded by Nik, and each polynomial row nonzero. Put X=∏i(Σj length(Pij)^2)^(1/2)·exp(Σk h(βk)Σi Nik). If n>mD, there is y∈ℤ^n nonzero with Σj γij yj=0 for all i and max|yj|≤X^(D/(n−mD)).
hypotheses: There are m rows and n unknowns; a zero evaluated row may simply be removed.
The input is the relative integer-solution theorem of ArithmeticHeights Layer 5.6, not a solution in OK.
proofSteps: Import the relative Bombieri–Vaaler theorem through DT.0’s height owner with base field ℚ. Its discriminant factor is 1.
Bound the absolute Arakelov height of each evaluated row by its Euclidean coefficient-length norm times the monomial height factors.
Multiply row bounds and take the geometric mean of the nonzero integer kernel vectors. Every rational integer vector height is its maximum coordinate magnitude.

nodes.title: Prime-power binomials with the dyadic hypothesis
nodes.statement: Let K have characteristic zero, q be prime, k≥1, and a∈K. If q=2 assume i∈K with i²=−1. Then X^(q^k)−a is irreducible if and only if a is not a q-th power in K. The odd-prime assertion is imported directly from Mathlib; only the dyadic consequence under i∈K is a new target.
hypotheses: The i hypothesis is mandatory when q=2.
If a=0 then a is a q-th power and the irreducibility assertion is false.
proofSteps: For q odd apply the pinned prime-power criterion.
For q=2 start with the pinned prime criterion and induct using X_pow_mul_sub_C_irreducible.
If a root β of X^(2^r)−a were a square in K(β), its norm would make −a a square in K. Since −1=i², this would make a a square, contradiction.
Conversely a=b^q gives the usual difference-of-powers factorization for k≥1.

sources.match: The prime-power criterion used for torsion roots includes i in the dyadic case.

acceptance: Over ℚ, X⁴+4 is reducible although −4 is not a square; hence the i hypothesis cannot be removed.
Over ℚ(i), −4=(2i)², so this example does not satisfy the non-square hypothesis.

nodes.title: The relation alternative for a prime-radical tower
nodes.statement: Let K have characteristic zero and contain all q-th roots of unity, q prime, αj∈Kˣ, and chosen θj with θj^q=αj. Put L=K(θ1,…,θr). For α∈Kˣ and θ^q=α, either [L(θ):L]=q or α=γ^q∏j αj^ij with γ∈Kˣ and 0≤ij<q. In the second case a q-th root is already in L. If the q-power classes of α1,…,αr are independent, the θ-monomials ∏θj^ij, 0≤ij<q, are a K-basis and [L:K]=q^r.
hypotheses: K contains μq; all radicals are taken in one algebraic closure.
The relation conclusion belongs to K; γ is not merely an element of L.
proofSteps: Apply the prime binomial criterion to the last extension.
The finite radical compositum is Galois; automorphisms embed into μq^r by their values on the chosen roots, using the pinned cyclic-binomial action at each irreducible step.
If θ∈L, its ratios σθ/θ form a character of this subgroup. A character extends to μq^r by elementary finite-field linear algebra. Divide θ by the corresponding θ-monomial.
The quotient is fixed by the full Galois group and hence lies in K. Taking q-th powers gives the displayed relation. For independent classes iterate and use the tower bases.

sources.match: The prime-radical relation is the algebraic input to descent from the full Kummer condition.

acceptance: For K=ℚ, q=2, α1=2, α=8, the relation is 8=2·2² and the new root is already in ℚ(√2).
For α1=2,α2=3 over ℚ the square classes are independent and the four radical monomials form a basis.
The base-field condition μq⊂K is retained in this adapter.

nodes.title: A monomial basis with bounded total degree
nodes.statement: Let F⊂K be a finite field extension of degree d generated by α1,…,αn. There is an F-basis consisting of monomials ∏j αj^kj with kj≥0 and Σkj≤d−1. In Yu’s setting F=ℚ(α0), [F:ℚ]=D0, [K:F]=D1, combine this basis with 1,α0,…,α0^(D0−1) to get a rational basis ξd0,d=α0^d0∏j αj^kjd, with 0≤d0<D0 and Σj kjd≤D1−1.
hypotheses: The αj generate the extension as a field and are algebraic over F.
α0 is a primitive torsion root in Yu’s application, so its powers form the indicated F/ℚ basis.
proofSteps: Let Vs be the span of monomials of total degree≤s. V0 has dimension 1.
If Vs=Vs+1, it is stable under all generator multiplications and contains their generated algebra; for algebraic generators that algebra is K.
Until Vs=K its dimension strictly increases. Therefore Vd−1=K. Extract a basis from this finite spanning set.
Use the ordinary tower basis and absolute-height monomial inequalities.

acceptance: The bound is on total degree, not on each exponent separately.
The actual basis may depend on α; the coefficient bound must be independent of its choice.

nodes.title: The effective house input used in the short-relation bound
nodes.statement: For a nonzero algebraic integer α of degree d that is not a root of unity, the height owner must supply log house(α)>1/(2d²). Consequently h(α)>1/(2d³). This is a quantitative hypothesis: Northcott and Kronecker alone do not yield this numerical constant. nodes.title: A bounded integer relation among dependent logarithms
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree D, and m≥2 chosen complex logarithms ℓ1,…,ℓm with exp ℓj∈Kˣ that are Q-linearly dependent. Choose Vj≥max(h(exp ℓj),|ℓj|/(2πD)), Vj>0. There are integers tj, not all zero, with Σj tjℓj=0 and |tk|≤[2(m−1)D³]^(m−1)∏j Vj/Vk for every k.
hypotheses: The dependence is among the chosen logarithms, retaining any 2πi contribution.
No division by a zero Vj is permitted.
proofSteps: Use the discrete lattice generated by logarithmic images modulo torsion and its rank-deficient relation map.

For a nonzero non-torsion algebraic integer, the effective-house input gives h>1/(2d³). For a nonintegral algebraic number of degree d, its primitive integer minimal polynomial has leading coefficient at least 2, hence h≥log 2/d>1/(2d³). Here d≤D. A torsion logarithm instead has zero height and its nonzero 2πi branch contribution must be retained explicitly in the logarithmic lattice.
Apply the geometry-of-numbers relation argument with the separate Vj weights; primitive scaling gives integer coefficients.
The cited Waldschmidt relation proof and Yu’s improved 2D² input have not been fully independently traced; record the exact missing supplier proof.

nodes.title: Torsion and deep-unit coordinates for Yu interpolation
nodes.statement: In the Yu unit setup put G=p^f−1, μ=ordq(G), G0=G/q^u, G1=G/q^μ, so G0=q^(μ−u)G1 and gcd(G1,q)=1. In K_P choose a primitive G-th root ζ with ζ^G0=α0^(p^v), and a q-th root ξ of ζ in an algebraic closure of K_P. Choose κ≥0 and residues 0≤rj<G with δj=αj^(p^κ)ζ^rj satisfying vp(δj−1)>θ+1/(p−1), θ>0 rational. Then log δj and exp(z log δj) are defined for integral z, and δj^(1/q)=exp(q⁻¹log δj). Choose compatible q-th roots of αj so δj^(1/q)=(αj^(1/q))^(p^κ)ξ^rj. For the analytic rescaling choose a finite complete extension E/K_P containing ξ, the compatible roots and an element aθ with vp(aθ)=θ. Such an element can be adjoined since θ is rational. Then exp(aθ⁻¹z log δj) is defined and normal on E’s closed unit disc.
hypotheses: K is a number field of degree D; P lies above p with ramification index e and residue degree f; n≥2.
Put q=3 when p=2 and q=2 otherwise. At p=2 assume ζ3∈K; at p≡1 mod4 assume i∈K; at p≡3 mod4 assume f odd or i∈K.
Let q^u and p^v be the largest q-power and p-power orders of roots of unity in K. Choose α0 primitive of order p^v q^u.
αj are P-units; θ>0 is rational and κ is large enough for the displayed strict inequality.
proofSteps: Use the residue-field multiplicative group and LocalFieldsRamification’s Teichmüller lift to choose ζ; match its q-primary part with α0^(p^v).
First multiply αj by a residue root to obtain a principal unit. Repeated p-th powering raises its order until it exceeds the chosen sharp threshold.
Apply the imported exponential/logarithm equivalence. Since q≠p, division by q preserves the analytic domain.

Adjust the chosen algebraic q-th roots by μq to match the analytic roots. Adjoin aθ with vp(aθ)=θ in a finite complete extension, so the strict inequality makes exp(aθ⁻¹z log δj) normal by the factorial valuation bound. The G0 and G1 definitions are checked before residue-class calculations. The extra analytic extension does not replace K in any arithmetic height or degree count.

The stronger depth estimate changes the scaling parameter, while retaining the compatible root construction.

nodes.title: Yu’s auxiliary interpolation functions
nodes.statement: Fix the torsion/deep-unit coordinates, box bounds Lj≥0 for −1≤j≤n, and a residue r modulo G1. Let C be the finite λ-box with Σj rjλj≡r mod G1. For integer coefficients pλ,d0,d and the bounded rational basis ξd0,d put pλ=Σd0,d pλ,d0,d ξd0,d. Define ΛJ(z,τ)=Δ(q^(−J)z+λ−1;L−1+1,λ0+1,τ0)∏j<n Δ(bnλj−bjλn;τj), and φJ(z,τ)=Σλ∈C pλΛJ(z,τ)∏j δj^(λjz). Split C into Ct by Σrjλj≡r+tG1 mod G0, 0≤t<q^(μ−u). Define φJ,t by the same φJ sum restricted to Ct. Put γλ,j=λj−(bj/bn)λn and fJ,t(z,τ)=Σλ∈Ct pλΛJ(z,τ)∏j<n δj^(γλ,j z). Here Δ(x;k,l,m) is the normalized derivative of Δ(x;k)^l, and Δ(x;t) denotes the rising-factorial polynomial.
hypotheses: J≥0; τ∈ℕ^n; the basis indices have 0≤d0<D0 and 1≤d≤D1.
bn has least p-order among the bj, so γλ,j is integral p-adically.
ΛJ depends on λ, including λ0+1; replacing that exponent by L0+1 would change the interpolation matrix.
proofSteps: Use finite sums, the existing number-field basis and the Delta polynomial adapter.
Restrict the finite box by the two congruences; G0=q^(μ−u)G1 makes Ct a disjoint partition.
Interpret all local powers via exp(z log δj) on the integral disc.
The least-order condition makes bj/bn integral; the resulting exponential factors are normal after the aθ⁻¹ rescaling in the finite complete extension specified by the torsion/deep-unit target.

nodes.title: A nonzero auxiliary function with small integer coefficients
nodes.statement: For each nonempty initial class Ct, take the algebraic equations φ0,t(s,τ)=0 with 1≤s≤S, q∤s, |τ|≤T. There are M0=(1−1/q)S binom(T+n,n) equations over K after dividing each row by its common local root-of-unity factor ζ^((r+tG1)s). With N0=D#Ct integer unknowns and N0>M0D, the relative Siegel polynomial-row bound gives a nonzero integer coefficient family of magnitude at most Xrow^(D/(N0−M0D)), where Xrow is the product of the Euclidean row-length and monomial-height bounds. If N0≥c0 M0D and Xrow≤X0^M0, its magnitude is at most X0^(1/(c0−1)). Join the independently solved Ct families to obtain the nonzero φ0 vanishing grid.
hypotheses: K is a number field of degree D; P lies above p with ramification index e and residue degree f; n≥2.
Put q=3 when p=2 and q=2 otherwise. At p=2 assume ζ3∈K; at p≡1 mod4 assume i∈K; at p≡3 mod4 assume f odd or i∈K.
Let q^u and p^v be the largest q-power and p-power orders of roots of unity in K. Choose α0 primitive of order p^v q^u.
Each αj, 1≤j≤n, is nonzero and a P-unit; bj∈ℤ, bn≠0 and vp(bn)=minj vp(bj); Θ=∏j αj^bj−1≠0.
Vj≥max(h(αj),f log p/D); V1≤⋯≤Vn−1; no ordering of Vn is required.

proofSteps: The basis coefficients give integer unknowns. In Ct, write Σrjλj=r+tG1+G0kλ. At an integer grid point s, the factor ζ^(sΣrjλj) equals the common unit ζ^((r+tG1)s) times (α0^(p^v))^(skλ), which belongs to K. Divide by the common unit before treating these as K-valued rows. Powers of ζ^(G1s) give the separate class independence by the prime-power binomial criterion.
Use the bounded monomial basis and Delta denominator bounds to express every row by integer polynomials after common denominator clearing.
Apply the relative Siegel row adapter to each class separately. Retain the exact product of row bounds instead of replacing it by the worst row.
Average the derivative index: Σ|τ|≤T τ0=binom(T+n,n+1). This is the saving in Yu 1994, Lemma 2.1.
Choose a nonzero solution for every nonempty class and join them; the basis independence ensures the joined algebraic coefficient family is nonzero.

nodes.title: Grid extrapolation and contraction of the auxiliary box
nodes.statement: Suppose the Yu unit setup and full Kummer condition hold, and vp(Θ)≥U. Starting with the small-coefficient auxiliary function, for 0≤J≤floor(log Ln/log q)+1 obtain a nonzero integer family with the same coefficient bound, L−1^(J)=L−1, L0^(J)=L0, 0≤Lj^(J)≤q^(−J)Lj for 1≤j≤n, and φJ(s,τ)=0 for 1≤s≤q^J S,q∤s,|τ|≤q^(−J)T. This assertion requires the explicit analytic/arithmetic budget conditions described below and the terminal nonvanishing conditions of the parameter-selection target.
hypotheses: K is a number field of degree D; P lies above p with ramification index e and residue degree f; n≥2.
Put q=3 when p=2 and q=2 otherwise. At p=2 assume ζ3∈K; at p≡1 mod4 assume i∈K; at p≡3 mod4 assume f odd or i∈K.
Let q^u and p^v be the largest q-power and p-power orders of roots of unity in K. Choose α0 primitive of order p^v q^u.
Each αj, 1≤j≤n, is nonzero and a P-unit; bj∈ℤ, bn≠0 and vp(bn)=minj vp(bj); Θ=∏j αj^bj−1≠0.
Vj≥max(h(αj),f log p/D); V1≤⋯≤Vn−1; no ordering of Vn is required.
The chosen q-th roots satisfy [K(α0^(1/q),…,αn^(1/q)):K]=q^(n+1).

The parameters satisfy the budget inequalities: at every J and k=0,…,n, set R=q^(J+k)S, M=floor((1−1/q)q^(−J)T/(n+1))+1, A=(L−1+1)(L0+1)(θ+1/(p−1)). In a finite complete extension containing aθ and a scalar cA with vp(cA)=A, the normalized jets of FJ,t(z,τ)=cA fJ,t(aθ⁻¹z,τ) have minimum order plus mθ at least (1−1/q)RMθ+Mvp(R!)+(M−1)log R/log p.

The difference φJ,t(y,τ)−fJ,t(y,τ) has order at least U−T log(L−1+1)/log p−vp(bn), for positive p-integral rational y. This lower bound and (1−1/q)RMθ−A both exceed the finite-place Liouville upper bound on each cleared nonzero algebraic evaluation, including evaluations in K(α0^(1/q),…,αn^(1/q)).
Ln≥1 for the displayed logarithmic terminal index. An initial Ln=0 box is treated directly by the terminal polynomial argument, whose precise grid/degree condition is recorded as a gap.
proofSteps: Induct on J. Within one J, extend the grid n times while reducing the derivative budget by (1−1/q)q^(−J)T/(n+1) at each step.

Differentiate the projected fJ,t and use the finite-difference identity for Delta: each normalized derivative is a controlled combination of nearby τ-indices. The normal-function Schwarz theorem applies with the displayed R,M,A.

Compare fJ,t to φJ,t using the small multiplicative form. At integer grid points first divide φJ,t by the common torsion unit ζ^((rJ+tG1)s); the remaining expression is a polynomial in α0,…,αn over K. At s/q use ξ^((rJ+tG1)s) instead, leaving a polynomial in the compatible q-th roots of α0,…,αn, of field degree q^(n+1)D. Clear the integer and q-power denominators using Yu 1994 Lemma 1.3, including its factorial q-order term. These root-of-unity factors have order zero. Finite-place Liouville applied in these arithmetic fields forces the grid values to vanish; the larger analytic field used to choose aθ,cA is not charged to those polynomial degrees.
At the fractional grid use the full radical monomial basis over K(ξ^G1). Its independence follows by the tower degree identity and the prime-power irreducibility of X^(q^(μ−u+1))−ζ_(q^u).

Write each exponent σj=λj*+qλj. Select a residue vector with a nonzero coefficient, retain that coefficient subfamily, and use the invertibility of q modulo G1 to define the next congruence. The bounds shrink by q while coefficient magnitudes do not grow.

At the terminal J, Ln^(J)=0. The finite-difference polynomial identities and the long grid force every retained coefficient to be zero, contradicting nonzero initialization. The untraced terminal argument imported from Yu 1989 is recorded as a gap.
